Look at the duplicate in `contacts.csv`. After I normalized case and whitespace in the email column and grouped by email, one address came up twice:

| Normalized email | Rows | Entries |
|---|---|---|
| `ana@example.org` | 2 | `Ana Ruiz, ana@example.org` and `ana ruiz, ANA@example.org` |
| `bo@example.org` | 1 | `Bo Lin, bo@example.org` |

The two Ana rows differ only in capitalization, so an exact-match dedupe missed them. Ana's address is on the list twice, which would explain the double newsletter.

The file has only 3 contacts, so this may be a sample. If the real list is bigger, run the same check on that one.

What to do next:
- **Dedupe before sending.** Lowercase and trim emails, then keep one row per address. Ideally do this wherever contacts are imported, so new duplicates don't get in.
- **Check the send side.** If the real list has no case-variant duplicates, the cause may be elsewhere, such as the newsletter job running twice or overlapping with another list. The `crontab.txt` and `app.log` in this directory are worth a look.
